nodes.label: Geometric constructions
nodes.title: Creating exact geometric figures using formal procedures with compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Applying geometric constructions to real-life contexts
nodes.title: Using constructions to solve practical layout, design, and measurement problems (e.g., bisecting spaces, setting right angles, laying out circles).

nodes.label: Drawing a circle of given radius
nodes.title: Using a compass set to a specified length to draw a circle centered at a point.

nodes.label: Use of a straightedge (unmarked ruler)
nodes.title: Drawing straight lines and extending segments without measurement.

nodes.label: Use of a compass
nodes.title: Transferring lengths and drawing arcs/circles for constructions.

nodes.label: Use of a ruler (measuring length)
nodes.title: Measuring and marking lengths accurately on diagrams.

nodes.label: Use of a protractor (measuring angles)
nodes.title: Measuring and marking angles to a required degree measure.

nodes.label: Use of a set square
nodes.title: Drawing perpendicular and specific-angle lines (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°) accurately.

nodes.label: Perpendicular bisector construction
nodes.title: Constructing the line that is perpendicular to a segment and passes through its midpoint using a compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Angle bisector construction
nodes.title: Constructing a ray that divides a given angle into two equal angles with compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Constructing a perpendicular line through a given point
nodes.title: Creating a line perpendicular to a given line either through a point on the line or a point not on the line.

nodes.label: Constructing a parallel line through a given point
nodes.title: Using compass-and-straightedge methods (e.g., corresponding angles) to draw a line parallel to a given line through a specified point.

nodes.label: Dynamic geometry software for constructions
nodes.title: Using digital tools (e.g., GeoGebra) to create, explore, and verify geometric constructions dynamically.

nodes.label: Precision and accuracy in geometric drawings
nodes.title: Applying correct instrument techniques to reduce error and produce exact constructions.

nodes.label: Cartesian coordinate plane
nodes.title: The two-dimensional plane defined by perpendicular x- and y-axes used to locate points with ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Ordered pairs (x, y)
nodes.title: A pair of numbers that uniquely identifies a point on the coordinate plane.

nodes.label: Plotting points on the coordinate plane
nodes.title: Placing points at given coordinates relative to the axes and origin.

nodes.label: Linear relationships in real-world contexts
nodes.title: Modeling real-life situations where one quantity changes at a constant rate with respect to another.

nodes.label: Tabular representation of linear relationships
nodes.title: Using value tables (x and corresponding y) to represent and analyze linear patterns.

nodes.label: Graphical representation of linear relationships
nodes.title: Plotting points and drawing straight lines to model linear functions on the coordinate plane.

nodes.label: Slope of a line
nodes.title: A measure of steepness of a line, often computed as rise over run (Δy/Δx).

nodes.label: Rate of change
nodes.title: Change in the dependent variable per unit change in the independent variable; constant for linear relationships.

nodes.label: Equivalence of slope and rate of change
nodes.title: Recognizing that the slope of a linear graph equals the contextual rate at which one quantity changes relative to another.

nodes.label: Y-intercept (start value)
nodes.title: The value of the dependent variable when the independent variable is zero; the initial value in context.

nodes.label: Interpreting intercepts in context
nodes.title: Explaining the meaning of the start value and other intercepts with respect to a real-world situation.

nodes.label: Comparing linear relationships
nodes.title: Analyzing and contrasting lines using slope (rate of change) and intercepts (start values).

nodes.label: Independent and dependent variables in linear models
nodes.title: Identifying which quantity is controlled (x) and which responds (y) in a linear relationship.

nodes.label: Point of intersection of two lines
nodes.title: The coordinate pair that satisfies both linear relationships simultaneously.

nodes.label: Interpreting intersection in context (break-even point)
nodes.title: Understanding the practical significance of where two linear models yield the same value.

nodes.label: Solving systems of linear equations by graphing
nodes.title: Finding the solution to two linear relationships by locating their point of intersection on a graph.

nodes.label: Graphical strategies for solving linear problems
nodes.title: Using graphs to estimate or determine solutions to linear equations and systems from context.

nodes.label: Numeric (tabular) strategies for solving linear problems
nodes.title: Using tables of values to compute, compare, and find solutions to linear relationships.

nodes.label: Mental strategies and estimation for linear problems
nodes.title: Estimating slopes, intercepts, and intersections to check reasonableness of solutions in context.

nodes.label: Right-angled triangles
nodes.title: Triangles with one 90° angle; sides include two legs and the hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Hypotenuse in a right triangle
nodes.title: The side opposite the right angle; the longest side of a right triangle.

nodes.label: Opposite and adjacent sides relative to an angle
nodes.title: Naming the leg opposite or adjacent to a given acute angle in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Pythagorean Theorem
nodes.title: In a right triangle, a^2 + b^2 = c^2, relating legs to the hypotenuse.

nodes.label: Applying the Pythagorean Theorem to heights and distances
nodes.title: Solving contextual right-triangle problems (e.g., ladders, buildings, line-of-sight) using a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios in right triangles
nodes.title: Definition of sine, cosine, and tangent as ratios of side lengths in a right triangle.

nodes.label: SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic
nodes.title: Mnemonic for remembering sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.

nodes.label: Selecting appropriate trigonometric ratio
nodes.title: Choosing sine, cosine, or tangent based on which sides are known and which are unknown.

nodes.label: Finding unknown side lengths using trigonometric ratios
nodes.title: Computing a missing leg or hypotenuse from an angle and a side using sine, cosine, or tangent.

nodes.label: Finding unknown angles using inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Using arcsin, arccos, or arctan to determine an angle from side-length ratios.

nodes.label: Angles of elevation and depression
nodes.title: Angles measured above or below a horizontal line used in real-world right-triangle models.

nodes.label: Modeling real-world situations with right triangles
nodes.title: Translating contextual scenarios (heights, distances, ramps, sightlines) into right-triangle diagrams.

nodes.label: Solving right triangles
nodes.title: Determining all unknown sides and angles using Pythagoras, trigonometric ratios, and inverse trig functions.

nodes.label: Transformation geometry
nodes.title: Study of geometric transformations and their properties in the plane.

nodes.label: Translation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: Shifts every point of a figure by the same vector, preserving distances and orientation.

nodes.label: Rotation (geometric transformation)
nodes.title: Turns a figure about a fixed center by a given angle, preserving distances and angles.

nodes.label: Axial symmetry (line reflection)
nodes.title: Reflection of a figure across a line (axis), producing a mirror image.

nodes.label: Central symmetry (point reflection)
nodes.title: A half-turn (180-degree rotation) about a point that maps each point to its opposite relative to the center.

nodes.label: Locating axes of symmetry in simple shapes
nodes.title: Identifying lines that divide a shape into two mirror-image halves.

nodes.label: Image under a transformation
nodes.title: The resulting point or figure after applying a specified geometric transformation.

nodes.label: Enlargement (dilation)
nodes.title: A similarity transformation that scales a figure from a center by a scale factor k > 0.

nodes.label: Centre of enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which distances are scaled along rays during an enlargement.

nodes.label: Scale factor of enlargement
nodes.title: The multiplicative factor k that scales all distances from the center in an enlargement.

nodes.label: Reduction (0 < k < 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor between 0 and 1 that produces a smaller similar image.

nodes.label: Magnification (k > 1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor greater than 1 that produces a larger similar image.

nodes.label: Rational scale factor (k ∈ Q)
nodes.title: Using rational numbers as scale factors in enlargements, including fractional scaling.

nodes.label: Area scaling under enlargement
nodes.title: Under an enlargement with scale factor k, the area of a figure scales by k^2.

nodes.label: Recognising images under transformations
nodes.title: Identifying the result of applying translations, rotations, axial symmetry, or central symmetry to points and shapes.

nodes.label: Solving problems involving enlargements
nodes.title: Applying center and scale factor to find images/preimages, lengths, and areas in enlargement contexts.

nodes.label: Rigid motions (isometries)
nodes.title: Transformations that preserve distances and angles, including translations, rotations, and reflections.

nodes.label: Synthetic geometry
nodes.title: Study of geometry using axioms, theorems, and constructions without coordinates or algebra.

nodes.label: Compass-and-straightedge constructions (16–21)
nodes.title: Perform a specified set of classical geometric constructions labeled 16–21 in the syllabus.

nodes.label: Compass-and-straightedge construction 22
nodes.title: Execute the syllabus' construction number 22 using a compass and straightedge.

nodes.label: Theorem (geometric)
nodes.title: A mathematical statement that can be proven from axioms and previously established results.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.title: A logically coherent argument establishing the truth of a theorem.

nodes.label: Axiom
nodes.title: A foundational assumption accepted without proof, used to derive theorems.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A proposition that follows readily from a theorem with little or no additional proof.

nodes.label: Converse of a statement
nodes.title: The statement formed by reversing the hypothesis and conclusion of an implication.

nodes.label: Logical implication (implies)
nodes.title: A relationship A → B meaning if A is true, then B must also be true.

nodes.label: Logical equivalence
nodes.title: Two statements that always have the same truth value; each implies the other.

nodes.label: Biconditional (if and only if)
nodes.title: The statement A iff B, asserting both A → B and B → A.

nodes.label: Proof by contradiction
nodes.title: An indirect proof technique that assumes the negation of the desired result and derives a contradiction.

nodes.label: Investigating geometric theorems through problem solving
nodes.title: Exploring, testing, and applying named theorems (e.g., 7, 8, 11–13, 16–18, 20–21) to solve geometric problems.

nodes.label: Corollary 6 (application in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: Use of a specified corollary labeled 6 in the syllabus to deduce further results and solve problems.

nodes.label: Theorem 11 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem concerning ratios in geometric figures, supporting later results.

nodes.label: Theorem 12 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem on ratios in geometry, forming part of the foundation for subsequent proofs.

nodes.label: Theorem 13 (ratios in synthetic geometry)
nodes.title: A syllabus theorem dealing with ratios in geometric contexts that underpins further results.

nodes.label: Geometric ratios and proportionality
nodes.title: Reasoning with ratios in geometric figures (e.g., segment lengths) to derive relationships and proofs.

nodes.label: Foundation for the Pythagorean theorem
nodes.title: Results and ratio arguments that prepare for the formal proof of the Pythagorean theorem.

nodes.label: Deductive reasoning in geometry
nodes.title: Deriving conclusions from axioms and theorems using logically valid steps.

nodes.label: Parallel lines criterion via slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.

nodes.label: Perpendicular lines criterion via slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes are negative reciprocals (m1 · m2 = -1).

nodes.label: Linear equation in general form (ax + by + c = 0)
nodes.title: Represents a straight line in the plane; coefficients determine slope and intercepts.

nodes.label: Angle between two lines using slopes
nodes.title: For slopes m1 and m2, tan(θ) = |(m1 − m2)/(1 + m1·m2)| gives the acute angle between lines.

nodes.label: Perpendicular distance from a point to a line
nodes.title: Distance from (x0, y0) to Ax + By + C = 0 is |Ax0 + By0 + C| / √(A2 + B2).

nodes.label: Internal division of a line segment (section formula)
nodes.title: Point dividing segment A(x1,y1) and B(x2,y2) internally in ratio m:n has coordinates ((mx2 + nx1)/(m+n), (my2 + ny1)/(m+n)).

nodes.label: Area of a triangle in the coordinate plane
nodes.title: Area with vertices (x1,y1),(x2,y2),(x3,y3) is 1/2 |x1(y2−y3) + x2(y3−y1) + x3(y1−y2)| (shoelace method).

nodes.label: Center-radius form of a circle equation
nodes.title: (x − h)2 + (y − k)2 = r2 represents all points at distance r from center (h, k).

nodes.label: General form of a circle equation
nodes.title: x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a circle with center (−g, −f) and radius r = √(g2 + f2 − c).

nodes.label: Equation of a circle centered at the origin
nodes.title: x2 + y2 = r2 describes a circle with center (0, 0) and radius r.

nodes.label: Line–circle intersection (center at origin)
nodes.title: Solving a line with x2 + y2 = r2 to find intersection points; includes cases of secant, tangent, or no intersection.

nodes.label: Line–circle intersection (general)
nodes.title: Solving simultaneous equations of a line and a circle to determine intersection points and tangency conditions.

nodes.label: Pythagorean theorem (2D)
nodes.title: In a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the legs equals the square of the hypotenuse (a^2 + b^2 = c^2); used to solve planar problems.

nodes.label: Area of a triangle using trigonometry
nodes.title: Compute area with A = (1/2)ab sin C when two sides and the included angle are known.

nodes.label: Sine rule (Law of sines)
nodes.title: Relates sides and angles in any triangle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C; used to find unknown sides/angles.

nodes.label: Cosine rule (Law of cosines)
nodes.title: Generalizes Pythagoras: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 − 2ab cos C (and cyclic forms) to find sides/angles in any triangle.

nodes.label: Definition of sin θ for all real θ
nodes.title: Extends sine to all real angles (e.g., via the unit circle), allowing positive/negative values and periodicity.

nodes.label: Definition of cos θ for all real θ
nodes.title: Extends cosine to all real angles (e.g., via the unit circle) with even symmetry and period 2π.

nodes.label: Definition of tan θ
nodes.title: Defines tangent as tan θ = sin θ / cos θ with undefined values where cos θ = 0; period π.

nodes.label: Area of a sector of a circle
nodes.title: Area given by A = (1/2) r^2 θ (radians) or A = (θ/360) π r^2 (degrees).

nodes.label: Arc length of a circle
nodes.title: Arc length given by s = r θ (radians) or s = (θ/360) 2π r (degrees).

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios in surd form
nodes.title: Use exact radical values for sin, cos, tan of special angles (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°) instead of decimals.

nodes.label: 3D trigonometry problem solving
nodes.title: Apply trigonometric methods to three-dimensional contexts to find lengths, angles, and distances.

nodes.label: Graph of y = sin θ
nodes.title: Sine function graph with amplitude 1, period 2π, and key intercepts/maximum/minimum points.

nodes.label: Graph of y = cos θ
nodes.title: Cosine function graph with amplitude 1, period 2π, starting at maximum when θ = 0.

nodes.label: Graph of y = tan θ
nodes.title: Tangent function graph with period π and vertical asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2.

nodes.label: Graphing transformed sine functions a + b sin(cθ)
nodes.title: Plot sinusoidal graphs with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Graphing transformed cosine functions a + b cos(cθ)
nodes.title: Plot cosine graphs with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: General solutions of trigonometric equations
nodes.title: Find all solutions using periodicity, e.g., sin(nθ) = 0 implies θ = kπ/n for integers k.

nodes.label: Solving equations like cos(nθ) = 1/2
nodes.title: Determine principal solutions and express the infinite family of solutions using k ∈ Z.

nodes.label: Radian measure of angles
nodes.title: Measure angles via arc length: θ = s/r; convert between degrees and radians and use radians in formulas.

nodes.label: Derivation of core trigonometric identities
nodes.title: Prove identities such as Pythagorean, angle addition/subtraction, and double-angle formulas.

nodes.label: Application of trigonometric identities
nodes.title: Use identities to simplify expressions, transform formulas, and solve trigonometric equations.

nodes.label: Reduction (0<k<1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor 0<k<1 that produces a smaller, similar image; all linear dimensions are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Magnification (k>1)
nodes.title: An enlargement with scale factor k>1 that produces a larger, similar image; all linear dimensions are multiplied by k.

nodes.label: Constructing an enlargement with given center and scale factor
nodes.title: A procedure using rays from the center through object points and proportional distances to draw the image at scale factor k.

nodes.label: Finding the centre of enlargement from object and image
nodes.title: A method to locate the center by joining pairs of corresponding points and intersecting the lines through them.

nodes.label: Relating linear and area scale factors
nodes.title: Understanding that linear measures scale by k while areas scale by k^2 in an enlargement.

nodes.title: Arranging items in rows and columns to represent products

nodes.label: Associative property

nodes.title: Using visual and contextual models to reason about operations on rational numbers

nodes.title: Transferring properties and operation meanings from whole numbers to rationals

nodes.label: Representing problems with diagrams
nodes.title: Using visual representations to model and solve contextual arithmetic problems

nodes.label: Solving problems with fractional amounts in context
nodes.title: Applying fraction operations to real-world scenarios

nodes.title: Observing regularities in operations and expressing them as general statements

nodes.title: Real numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers; have non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansions.

nodes.title: Understanding that the set of real numbers strictly contains the rationals; not all real numbers are rational.

nodes.title: Performing arithmetic, estimation, and simplification with numbers involving radicals and other irrationals.

nodes.label: Arithmetic operations in natural numbers (N)
nodes.title: Using addition and multiplication within the natural numbers and recognizing closure and basic properties.

nodes.label: Arithmetic operations in integers (Z)
nodes.title: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division (with remainders) in the domain of integers and closure properties.

nodes.label: Arithmetic operations in rational numbers (Q)
nodes.title: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing fractions and mixed numbers, including simplification.

nodes.label: Arithmetic operations in real numbers (R)
nodes.title: Carrying out the four operations with decimals, radicals, and other real numbers while maintaining precision.

nodes.title: Multiplying complex numbers using distributive property and the identity i^2 = -1.

nodes.label: Division of complex numbers (rectangular form)

nodes.title: Graphical representation of complex numbers on the plane with real and imaginary axes.

nodes.label: Modulus of a complex number
nodes.title: The distance of a complex number from the origin in the Argand plane, |a+ib| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2).

nodes.label: Complex conjugate
nodes.title: For z = a + ib, the conjugate is a − ib; used in division and to find moduli.

nodes.label: Conjugate identities for sums and products
nodes.title: Properties: conj(z + w) = conj(z) + conj(w) and conj(zw) = conj(z)·conj(w).

nodes.title: Demonstrating that sqrt(2) cannot be written as a ratio of integers, typically by contradiction.

nodes.title: Interpreting terminating and recurring decimals as rational numbers and converting between forms.

nodes.label: Place value in the decimal system
nodes.title: Understanding digit value by position to read, write, and operate with decimals.

nodes.title: Determining divisors and multiples of natural numbers and using them in problem solving.

nodes.label: Prime numbers
nodes.title: Natural numbers greater than 1 with exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

nodes.label: Prime factorization
nodes.title: Expressing a number as a product of prime factors, unique up to order.

nodes.label: Scientific notation (standard form)
nodes.title: Writing numbers as a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10 and n ∈ Z for efficient representation of magnitude.

nodes.label: Arithmetic with numbers in scientific notation
nodes.title: Performing addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division while maintaining standard form.

nodes.label: Verifying formulae from number patterns
nodes.title: Observing patterns, conjecturing general formulas, and justifying them with appropriate reasoning.

nodes.label: Geometric sequences
nodes.title: Sequences with constant ratio between successive terms; nth term formula a r^(n−1).

nodes.title: Proof technique using a base case and inductive step to establish statements for all integers n.

nodes.label: Inductive proof of finite geometric series formula
nodes.title: Using induction to prove S_n = a(1 − r^n)/(1 − r) for r ≠ 1.

nodes.title: Using induction to establish an exponential function eventually dominates a quadratic.

nodes.title: Demonstrating factorial growth outpaces exponential base 2 via induction.

nodes.title: Recognizing standard forms (e.g., 1/n → 0, r^n → 0 for |r| < 1) without formal computation.

nodes.label: Limit of r^n for |r| < 1 as n → ∞

nodes.label: Deriving infinite geometric sum via limit of partial sums
nodes.title: Proving S_∞ by taking the limit of S_n = a(1 − r^n)/(1 − r) as n → ∞ for |r| < 1.
nodes.broader_concept: Sum to infinity of a geometric series

nodes.title: Modeling repeating decimals as sums of geometric series to convert to fractions.

nodes.label: Analysis of solution strategies
nodes.title: Evaluating and comparing different methods for solving a mathematical problem.

nodes.label: Percentage calculation
nodes.title: Finding a percentage of a quantity and expressing a quantity as a percentage of another.

nodes.title: Using fractions, decimals, or percentages to determine which of two or more proportions is larger or smaller.

nodes.label: Factors in the natural numbers (N)
nodes.title: Identifying whole-number factors of a given natural number.

nodes.label: Multiples in the natural numbers (N)
nodes.title: Recognizing and generating multiples of a given natural number.

nodes.label: Prime numbers in the natural numbers (N)
nodes.title: Identifying prime numbers and distinguishing them from composite numbers.

nodes.label: Relationship between ratio and proportion
nodes.title: Understanding that a proportion is an equality of two ratios and using this relationship to solve problems.

nodes.label: Order of magnitude check
nodes.title: Assessing whether a result is reasonable by comparing its size to expected powers of ten or benchmark values.

nodes.label: Working backwards (inverse reasoning)
nodes.title: Solving problems by reversing the steps of a process to check or find a solution.

nodes.label: Rounding results to a specified degree of accuracy
nodes.title: Adjusting a numerical answer to a required precision before reporting it.

nodes.label: Rounding to decimal places
nodes.title: Rounding a decimal number to a specified number of places to the right of the decimal point.

nodes.label: Rounding to significant figures
nodes.title: Expressing a number with a specified number of meaningful digits to reflect measurement precision.

nodes.label: Estimation of calculations
nodes.title: Making quick, approximate computations to gauge the size or reasonableness of results.

nodes.label: Approximation methods
nodes.title: Using simplified values or methods to obtain near-exact results when exact calculation is unnecessary.

nodes.label: Presenting numerical answers with specified accuracy
nodes.title: Reporting results clearly with the precision requested (e.g., to a given number of decimal places or significant figures).

nodes.label: Expressing non-zero positive rational numbers in scientific notation
nodes.title: Converting positive rational numbers to the normalized form a*10^n where n is an integer and 1 ≤ a < 10.

nodes.label: Powers of ten with integer exponents
nodes.title: Understanding and using 10^n for integer n to scale numbers and interpret place value shifts.

nodes.label: Square numbers (a^2)
nodes.title: Representing and computing the square of a number as a × a.

nodes.label: Cube numbers (a^3)
nodes.title: Representing and computing the cube of a number as a × a × a.

nodes.label: Square root of a number (√a or a^{1/2})
nodes.title: Interpreting and calculating the principal square root and linking it to fractional indices.

nodes.label: Reciprocal of a number (1/a or a^{-1})
nodes.title: Understanding and computing the multiplicative inverse of a nonzero number and its expression using negative indices.

nodes.label: Index (exponent) notation
nodes.title: Using powers to represent repeated multiplication and to encode squares, cubes, roots, and reciprocals.

nodes.label: Fractional indices (a^{1/2})
nodes.title: Interpreting fractional exponents as roots, specifically that a^{1/2} equals √a.

nodes.label: Negative indices (a^{-1})
nodes.title: Understanding that negative exponents represent reciprocals, e.g., a^{-1} = 1/a for a ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Converting between radical and exponential forms
nodes.title: Rewriting expressions like √a as a^{1/2} and 1/a as a^{-1} to switch between radicals and indices.

nodes.label: Evaluating squares, cubes, and square roots of integers
nodes.title: Calculating exact values for a^2, a^3, and √a (when a is a perfect square), and recognizing common results.

nodes.label: Solving contextual problems with powers, roots, and reciprocals
nodes.title: Applying squares, cubes, square roots, and reciprocals to real-world and word problems.

nodes.label: Rule-based generation of sequences
nodes.title: Understanding that a process or rule (algorithm) can generate a sequence of numbers or objects.

nodes.label: Pattern investigation in sequences
nodes.title: Exploring and analyzing regularities in sequences, including examining differences, ratios, and structure.

nodes.label: Sequence continuation using patterns
nodes.title: Extending a sequence by applying the identified rule or pattern to find subsequent terms.

nodes.label: Algebraic generalisation of patterns
nodes.title: Expressing observed patterns using variables and algebraic expressions or formulas.

nodes.label: Position-to-term rule (explicit nth-term formula)
nodes.title: Writing a formula a_n that gives the nth term of a sequence directly as a function of n.

nodes.label: Term-to-term rule (recursive definition)
nodes.title: Defining each term of a sequence based on previous term(s), e.g., a_{n+1} in terms of a_n.

nodes.label: Arithmetic sequence (arithmetic progression)
nodes.title: A sequence where consecutive terms differ by a constant difference d; a_n = a_1 + (n−1)d.

nodes.label: Common difference of an arithmetic sequence
nodes.title: The constant amount d added to each term to get the next in an arithmetic sequence.

nodes.label: Geometric sequence (geometric progression)
nodes.title: A sequence where each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a constant ratio r; a_n = a_1 r^{n−1}.

nodes.label: Common ratio of a geometric sequence
nodes.title: The constant factor r by which each term is multiplied to obtain the next term in a geometric sequence.

nodes.label: Classifying sequences as arithmetic, geometric, or neither
nodes.title: Determining the type of a sequence by testing for constant differences (arithmetic) or constant ratios (geometric).

nodes.label: Arithmetic series
nodes.title: The sum of the terms of an arithmetic sequence.

nodes.label: Sum to n terms of an arithmetic series (S_n)
nodes.title: Computing S_n using S_n = n/2 [2a_1 + (n−1)d].

nodes.label: Sum to n terms using first and last terms
nodes.title: Using S_n = n/2 (first term + nth term) to compute the partial sum of an arithmetic series.

nodes.label: Partial sum notation (S_n)
nodes.title: Using S_n to denote the sum of the first n terms of a sequence or series.

nodes.label: Product of Powers (Same Base)
nodes.title: Multiply powers with the same base by adding exponents: a^p · a^q = a^(p+q).

nodes.label: Quotient of Powers (Same Base)
nodes.title: Divide powers with the same base by subtracting exponents: a^p / a^q = a^(p−q).

nodes.label: Zero Exponent Rule
nodes.title: Any nonzero base raised to the zero power equals 1: a^0 = 1.

nodes.label: Power of a Power
nodes.title: Raise a power to a power by multiplying exponents: (a^p)^q = a^(pq).

nodes.label: Negative Exponents
nodes.title: A negative exponent denotes a reciprocal: a^(−p) = 1/a^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Product
nodes.title: Distribute the exponent over a product: (ab)^p = a^p b^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Quotient
nodes.title: Distribute the exponent over a quotient: (a/b)^p = a^p / b^p.

nodes.label: Fractional Exponents as Roots
nodes.title: A fractional index of 1/q denotes a q-th root: a^(1/q) = √[q]{a} (for a > 0).

nodes.label: Rational Exponents
nodes.title: Interpret a^(p/q) as q-th root of a^p and as (q-th root of a)^p: a^(p/q) = √[q]{a^p} = (√[q]{a})^p.

nodes.label: Domain Restrictions for Indices
nodes.title: Understand when expressions with exponents are real, e.g., a ≠ 0 for negative exponents; a > 0 for fractional exponents with even denominators; p,q ∈ ℚ as specified.

nodes.label: Simplifying Expressions Using Index Laws
nodes.title: Apply exponent rules to simplify algebraic expressions involving powers.

nodes.label: Logarithm Product Rule
nodes.title: Logarithm of a product is the sum of logarithms: log_a(xy) = log_a x + log_a y.

nodes.label: Logarithm Quotient Rule
nodes.title: Logarithm of a quotient is the difference of logarithms: log_a(x/y) = log_a x − log_a y.

nodes.label: Logarithm Power Rule
nodes.title: An exponent becomes a multiplier: log_a(x^q) = q · log_a x.

nodes.label: Logarithm of Base and One
nodes.title: Evaluate key logarithms: log_a a = 1 and log_a 1 = 0.

nodes.label: Change of Base Formula
nodes.title: Convert between logarithm bases: log_a x = (log_b x)/(log_b a).

nodes.label: Domain and Base Restrictions for Logarithms
nodes.title: Recognize valid inputs: base a > 0, a ≠ 1; argument x > 0.

nodes.label: Solving Problems Using Logarithm and Exponent Laws
nodes.title: Use laws of indices and logarithms to simplify expressions and solve equations.

nodes.label: Number sequences
nodes.title: Ordered lists of numbers generated by a rule or process.

nodes.label: Sequence generation by processes
nodes.title: Creating sequences from iterative rules or procedures applied repeatedly.

nodes.label: Pattern recognition in sequences
nodes.title: Identifying regularities or relationships among terms in a sequence.

nodes.label: Continuing a sequence using a pattern
nodes.title: Using identified rules to predict and extend subsequent terms.

nodes.label: Algebraic generalization of patterns
nodes.title: Expressing observed patterns using variables and algebraic expressions.

nodes.label: nth-term formula for a sequence
nodes.title: An explicit expression that gives the nth term of a sequence.

nodes.label: Arithmetic sequence
nodes.title: A sequence where consecutive terms differ by a constant common difference.

nodes.label: Common difference
nodes.title: The fixed amount added to each term to obtain the next term in an arithmetic sequence.

nodes.label: Explicit formula for arithmetic sequence
nodes.title: Formula a_n = a_1 + (n − 1)d giving the nth term from first term and common difference.

nodes.label: Geometric sequence
nodes.title: A sequence where each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a constant common ratio.

nodes.label: Common ratio
nodes.title: The fixed factor by which consecutive terms of a geometric sequence differ.

nodes.label: Explicit formula for geometric sequence
nodes.title: Formula a_n = a_1 r^(n − 1) giving the nth term from first term and common ratio.

nodes.label: Series and partial sums
nodes.title: The sum of terms of a sequence, especially the sum of the first n terms.

nodes.label: Sum to n terms of an arithmetic series
nodes.title: Using S_n = n/2 [2a_1 + (n − 1)d] to find the partial sum of an arithmetic series.

nodes.label: Recursive definition of a sequence
nodes.title: Defining each term based on previous term(s) and an initial value.

nodes.label: Pattern generalization with variables
nodes.title: Using variables to write rules that model numerical or visual patterns.

nodes.label: Visual or object sequences
nodes.title: Sequences formed by arrangements of shapes or objects following a rule.

nodes.label: Predicting future terms of a sequence
nodes.title: Using the identified rule or formula to determine later terms.

nodes.label: Product rule for exponents (a^p · a^q = a^(p+q))
nodes.title: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents.

nodes.label: Quotient rule for exponents (a^p / a^q = a^(p−q))
nodes.title: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.

nodes.label: Zero exponent rule (a^0 = 1, a ≠ 0)
nodes.title: Any nonzero base raised to the zero power equals one.

nodes.label: Power of a power rule ((a^p)^q = a^(pq))
nodes.title: When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents.

nodes.label: Negative exponent rule (a^(−p) = 1/a^p)
nodes.title: A negative exponent represents the reciprocal of the positive exponent.

nodes.label: Power of a product rule ((ab)^p = a^p b^p)
nodes.title: A product raised to a power equals the product of each factor raised to that power.

nodes.label: Power of a quotient rule ((a/b)^p = a^p / b^p, b ≠ 0)
nodes.title: A quotient raised to a power equals the quotient of each term raised to that power.

nodes.label: Fractional exponent as root (a^(1/q) is the qth root of a)
nodes.title: A power with exponent 1/q equals the qth root of the base (for real numbers, typically a > 0, q ≠ 0).

nodes.label: Rational exponents (a^(p/q) = (qth root of a)^p = qth root of a^p)
nodes.title: A rational exponent represents a root and a power, with domain restrictions such as a > 0 for real roots when q is even.

nodes.label: Domain restrictions for exponent rules
nodes.title: Understanding conditions like a, b ≠ 0; q ≠ 0; and a > 0 when roots or logarithms are involved, to ensure results are real.

nodes.label: Product rule for logarithms (log_a(xy) = log_a x + log_a y)
nodes.title: The logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms.

nodes.label: Quotient rule for logarithms (log_a(x/y) = log_a x − log_a y)
nodes.title: The logarithm of a quotient is the difference of the logarithms.

nodes.label: Power rule for logarithms (log_a(x^q) = q log_a x)
nodes.title: An exponent on the argument can be brought down as a multiplier.

nodes.label: Special logarithm values (log_a a = 1 and log_a 1 = 0)
nodes.title: Logarithm of the base equals one; logarithm of one equals zero for any valid base a.

nodes.label: Change of base formula (log_a x = log_b x / log_b a)
nodes.title: Allows computation of logarithms in any base using a different base, such as common or natural logs.

nodes.label: Applying exponent laws in problem solving
nodes.title: Use index rules to simplify expressions and solve equations involving powers.

nodes.label: Applying logarithm laws in problem solving
nodes.title: Use logarithmic identities to simplify expressions and solve logarithmic and exponential equations.

nodes.label: Value-added tax (VAT) calculation

nodes.label: Currency conversion with exchange rates and commission

nodes.label: Two-part tariff pricing (fixed fee plus per-unit rate)

nodes.label: Ratio simplification

nodes.label: Unitary method for proportion problems

nodes.label: Direct proportion problems
nodes.title: Model relationships of the form y = kx and solve for unknowns using constant ratios.

nodes.label: Measurement unit conversion (metric)
nodes.title: Convert between metric units of length, mass, and capacity using powers of 10.

nodes.label: Timetable interpretation and elapsed time
nodes.title: Read timetables and calculate departure, arrival, and duration of journeys.

nodes.title: Use relationships speed = distance ÷ time, distance = speed × time, and time = distance ÷ speed.

nodes.label: Rate unit conversion (e.g., km/h to m/s)
nodes.title: Convert rate units to maintain consistency when solving speed–distance–time problems.

nodes.title: Apply A = P(1 + r)^n to compute accumulated amount for up to three compounding periods.

nodes.label: Income tax at standard rate
nodes.title: Calculate tax payable by applying a single flat rate to taxable income.

nodes.label: Net pay calculation with fixed deductions
nodes.title: Find net pay from gross pay by subtracting income tax and specified deductions.

nodes.label: Meter reading and consumption cost calculation
nodes.title: Compute utility usage from meter readings and determine cost using given rates.

nodes.label: Shopping total cost calculation
nodes.title: Calculate the total cost of multiple items, incorporating discounts or taxes when applicable.

nodes.label: Nets of Rectangular Prisms
nodes.title: Flattened 2D layouts of a rectangular solid that fold to form the 3D prism; used to analyze faces and compute surface area.

nodes.label: Nets of Cylinders
nodes.title: A rectangle (lateral surface) with two congruent circles (bases) that fold to form a cylinder; supports surface area calculations.

nodes.label: Using Nets to Compute Surface Area
nodes.title: Procedure of laying out all faces of a solid as a net, finding each face’s area, and summing to get total surface area.

nodes.label: Distinguishing Surface Area and Volume
nodes.title: Understanding that surface area measures the total exterior area of a 3D object while volume measures the space it occupies.

nodes.label: Distinguishing Perimeter and Area
nodes.title: Recognizing perimeter as the length around a 2D figure and area as the measure of the region it covers.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a Triangle
nodes.title: Sum of the lengths of the three sides of a triangle.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a Rectangle
nodes.title: P = 2(l + w) for a rectangle with length l and width w.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a Square
nodes.title: P = 4s for a square with side length s.

nodes.label: Circumference of a Circle
nodes.title: The perimeter of a circle; C = 2πr or C = πd.

nodes.label: Pi (π) as Circumference–Diameter Ratio
nodes.title: The constant π is the ratio of a circle’s circumference to its diameter.

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle
nodes.title: A = 1/2 bh, where b is base and h is corresponding height.

nodes.label: Area of a Rectangle
nodes.title: A = l × w for a rectangle with length l and width w.

nodes.label: Area of a Square
nodes.title: A = s^2 for a square with side length s.

nodes.label: Area of a Circle (Disc)
nodes.title: A = πr^2 for a circle of radius r.

nodes.label: Area of Composite Shapes by Decomposition
nodes.title: Finding the area of figures composed of basic shapes by partitioning into known shapes and summing areas.

nodes.label: Perimeter of Composite Figures
nodes.title: Determining the total boundary length of shapes formed by combining basic figures, accounting for shared edges.

nodes.label: Estimating Area of Irregular Shapes
nodes.title: Using strategies such as grid approximation and decomposition to approximate area when formulas do not directly apply.

nodes.label: Volume of a Rectangular Prism
nodes.title: V = lwh, the product of length, width, and height.

nodes.label: Surface Area of a Rectangular Prism
nodes.title: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh), the sum of the areas of all six faces.

nodes.label: Volume of a Cylinder
nodes.title: V = πr^2h, where r is the radius of the base and h is height.

nodes.label: Surface Area of a Cylinder
nodes.title: SA = 2πrh + 2πr^2, sum of lateral area and areas of two bases.

nodes.label: Volume of a Sphere
nodes.title: V = 4/3 πr^3 for a sphere of radius r.

nodes.label: Surface Area of a Sphere
nodes.title: SA = 4πr^2 for a sphere of radius r.

nodes.label: Scaled Diagrams and Scale Factor
nodes.title: Drawing and interpreting diagrams to scale, using a constant scale factor to relate drawing measurements to real sizes.

nodes.label: Mathematical Modeling with Surface Area and Volume
nodes.title: Formulating and solving real-world problems that involve selecting appropriate formulas and units for surface area and volume.

nodes.label: Multi-step Problem Solving in Measurement
nodes.title: Solving problems requiring multiple stages, such as combining area and perimeter or linking nets, surface area, and volume.

nodes.label: Working backwards to verify solutions
nodes.title: Use inverse operations or reverse reasoning to confirm the correctness of a result.

nodes.label: Rounding of numerical results
nodes.title: Round answers to a specified degree of accuracy to simplify or report results appropriately.

nodes.label: Error accumulation in sums and differences
nodes.title: Propagate measurement errors when adding or subtracting quantities by adding absolute errors.

nodes.label: Estimation and approximation of calculations
nodes.title: Make and justify rough calculations to obtain quick, reasonable answers.

nodes.label: Percentage error
nodes.title: Compute the relative error as a percentage of the true or accepted value.

nodes.label: Tolerance in measurements
nodes.title: Specify acceptable limits of variation around a target measurement.

nodes.label: Average rate of change with respect to time
nodes.title: Calculate change in a quantity per unit time using Δquantity/Δtime.

nodes.label: Cost price calculation
nodes.title: Determine the original cost of goods before profit, loss, or discounts.

nodes.label: Selling price calculation
nodes.title: Compute the final price at which goods are sold, including adjustments like markups or discounts.

nodes.label: Discount calculation
nodes.title: Find the reduction from list price using a percentage discount and compute the discounted price.

nodes.label: Markup (profit as percentage of cost price)
nodes.title: Express profit as a percentage of cost to set a selling price.

nodes.label: Margin (profit as percentage of selling price)
nodes.title: Express profit as a percentage of the selling price to assess profitability.

nodes.label: Compound interest calculations
nodes.title: Calculate accumulated value using repeated percentage growth, typically A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt).

nodes.label: Reducing balance (declining balance) depreciation
nodes.title: Model asset value decreasing by a fixed percentage each period.

nodes.label: Income tax calculation
nodes.title: Compute tax owed based on income and applicable rates or brackets.

nodes.label: Net pay calculation with deductions
nodes.title: Determine take-home pay after income tax and other deductions.

nodes.label: Materials costing
nodes.title: Estimate total material costs based on quantities, unit prices, and waste factors.

nodes.label: Labour costing
nodes.title: Calculate labour costs using hours worked and wage rates, including overtime if applicable.

nodes.label: Wastage allowance in costing
nodes.title: Include an additional percentage or amount to account for expected waste of materials.

nodes.label: Metric system units
nodes.title: Use SI base and derived units and their prefixes for measurement.

nodes.label: Unit conversion (metric and imperial)
nodes.title: Convert quantities between units using provided conversion factors.

nodes.label: Estimation of real-world measures
nodes.title: Make reasonable estimates of lengths, masses, times, and other physical quantities in context.

nodes.label: Present value
nodes.title: Determine the current worth of a future amount of money using a discount rate.

nodes.label: Loan repayment using present value (annuity method)
nodes.title: Use present value of an annuity to compute periodic loan repayments.

nodes.label: Investment valuation using present value
nodes.title: Apply discounting to evaluate the present value of future investment cash flows.

nodes.label: Nets of prisms
nodes.title: 2D layouts that fold to form prisms; used to visualize and compute surface area.

nodes.label: Net of a cylinder
nodes.title: Unfolded form of a cylinder consisting of a rectangle and two congruent circles.

nodes.label: Net of a right cone
nodes.title: Unfolded form of a right cone consisting of a sector and a circle.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a parallelogram
nodes.title: P = 2(a + b) for adjacent side lengths a and b.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a trapezium
nodes.title: Sum of all four side lengths of a trapezium.

nodes.label: Perimeter of a sector of a circle
nodes.title: Sum of arc length and two radii: P = rθ + 2r (radians) or P = (θ/360)·2πr + 2r (degrees).

nodes.label: Area of a parallelogram
nodes.title: A = b·h where h is the perpendicular height to base b.

nodes.label: Area of a trapezium
nodes.title: A = 1/2·(a + b)·h where a and b are parallel sides and h is height.

nodes.label: Arc length of a sector
nodes.title: L = rθ (radians) or L = (θ/360)·2πr (degrees).

nodes.label: Area and perimeter of composite plane figures
nodes.title: Decompose or combine standard shapes to find total area and perimeter.

nodes.label: Surface area of a rectangular block (cuboid)
nodes.title: Sum of areas of six rectangular faces; SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).

nodes.label: Volume of a rectangular block (cuboid)
nodes.title: V = l·w·h.

nodes.label: Surface area of a right cone
nodes.title: Total SA = πrl + πr^2; curved area = πrl where l is slant height.

nodes.label: Surface area of a triangular prism
nodes.title: Sum of areas of two triangular bases and three rectangular faces.

nodes.label: Volume of a triangular prism
nodes.title: V = (area of triangular base) × (prism length).

nodes.label: Surface area of a hemisphere
nodes.title: Total SA = 3πr^2; curved area = 2πr^2.

nodes.label: Surface area and volume of composite solids
nodes.title: Decompose or combine standard solids to compute total surface area and volume.

nodes.label: Trapezoidal rule for area approximation
nodes.title: Numerical method approximating area under a curve using trapezia; A ≈ h/2 [y0 + 2Σy_i + y_n].

nodes.label: Investigate nets to determine surface area
nodes.title: Use and analyze nets to derive and justify surface area formulas of solids.

nodes.label: Identifying triangle types: right, isosceles, equilateral
nodes.title: Classify triangles by side and angle properties to select appropriate formulas in problems.

nodes.label: Polynomial expression
nodes.title: Algebraic expressions consisting of sums of terms with variables raised to non-negative integer powers.

nodes.label: Degree of a polynomial
nodes.title: The highest power (exponent) of the variable in a polynomial expression.

nodes.label: Binomial
nodes.title: A polynomial expression with exactly two terms.

nodes.label: Trinomial
nodes.title: A polynomial expression with exactly three terms.

nodes.label: Coefficient
nodes.title: The numerical factor multiplied by the variable term in an algebraic expression.

nodes.label: Addition and subtraction of polynomials
nodes.title: Combining like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients.

nodes.label: Multiplying polynomial expressions
nodes.title: Applying distributive property to multiply each term in one polynomial by each term in another.

nodes.label: Expansion of bracketed polynomial expressions
nodes.title: Expressing products of polynomials as sums by multiplying out parentheses.

nodes.label: Perfect square trinomial
nodes.title: A trinomial that is the square of a binomial of the form $(x \pm a)^2$.

nodes.label: Difference of two squares
nodes.title: Identity stating that $(x - a)(x + a) = x^2 - a^2$.

nodes.label: Dividing algebraic expressions
nodes.title: Simplifying algebraic fractions by factoring and performing polynomial division where necessary.

nodes.label: Polynomial long division
nodes.title: Algorithm for dividing polynomials similar to numerical long division.

nodes.label: Polynomial functions
nodes.title: Functions defined by polynomial expressions where the input is substituted into the polynomial.

nodes.label: Evaluating polynomial functions
nodes.title: Determining the value of a polynomial function by substituting a numerical input.

nodes.label: Algebraic factor
nodes.title: An expression that divides a polynomial evenly leaving no remainder.

nodes.label: Highest common factor (HCF)
nodes.title: The largest algebraic expression which divides two or more expressions.

nodes.label: Factorization by grouping
nodes.title: Technique to factorize polynomials by grouping terms with common factors.

nodes.label: Factorization of difference of two squares
nodes.title: Factoring expressions of the form $a^2 - b^2$ as $(a-b)(a+b)$.

nodes.label: Factorizing quadratic polynomials
nodes.title: Writing quadratic polynomials in factored form as product of two binomials.

nodes.label: Factor theorem
nodes.title: If $f(k)=0$, then $(x-k)$ is a factor of the polynomial $f(x)$.

nodes.label: Partial fractions
nodes.title: Expressing rational algebraic expressions as sum of simpler fractions.

nodes.label: Manipulating formulae
nodes.title: Rearranging formulae to make a specified variable the subject.

nodes.label: Algebraic inequalities
nodes.title: Inequalities involving algebraic expressions and their solution sets.

nodes.label: Solving linear equations
nodes.title: Finding the value(s) of variables that satisfy linear equations.

nodes.label: Solving quadratic equations
nodes.title: Finding roots of quadratic equations using factorization, formula, or graphing.

nodes.label: Simultaneous linear equations with two variables
nodes.title: Solving systems of two linear equations to find values of two unknowns.

nodes.label: Simultaneous linear equations with three variables
nodes.title: Solving systems of three linear equations to find three unknowns.

nodes.label: Radian measure
nodes.title: Measurement of angles as ratio of arc length to radius in a circle.

nodes.label: Trigonometric ratios
nodes.title: Ratios of sides in right triangles: sine, cosine, tangent.

nodes.label: Trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Functions sine, cosine, tangent defined over angles.

nodes.label: The Sine Rule
nodes.title: Relationship between sides and sines of opposite angles of any triangle: $a/\sin A = b/\sin B = c/\sin C$.

nodes.label: The Cosine Rule
nodes.title: Law relating sides and included angle of triangle: $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc \cos A$.

nodes.label: Graphs of trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Plots of sine, cosine and tangent showing periodic behavior, amplitude, range and asymptotes.

nodes.label: Related trigonometric graphs
nodes.title: Transformations affecting amplitude, period, phase shift and midline of trig graphs.

nodes.label: Sequences
nodes.title: Ordered lists of numbers defined by patterns or formulas.

nodes.label: Arithmetic sequences
nodes.title: Sequences with a constant difference between consecutive terms.

nodes.label: Geometric series
nodes.title: Sum of terms of a geometric sequence, with formula for finite n terms and sum to infinity when $|r|<1$.

nodes.label: Recurrence relations
nodes.title: Sequences where each term is defined as a function of preceding terms.

nodes.label: Number patterns
nodes.title: Identifying sequence growth via finite differences and matching to polynomial functions (linear/quadratic/cubic).

nodes.label: Equation of a line - slope-intercept form
nodes.title: Line expressed as $y = mx + c$, with slope $m$ and $y$-intercept $c$.

nodes.label: Equation of a line - point-slope form
nodes.title: Equation of a line given a point and slope: $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$.

nodes.label: Parallel lines and slopes
nodes.title: Lines are parallel if they have equal slopes.

nodes.label: Perpendicular lines and slopes
nodes.title: Two lines are perpendicular if the product of their slopes is -1.

nodes.label: Distance between two points
nodes.title: Distance formula: $\sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$.

nodes.label: Midpoint of a line segment
nodes.title: Coordinates of midpoint: $\left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)$.

nodes.label: Angle between two lines
nodes.title: The angle $\theta$ between lines with slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ is given by $\tan \theta = |(m_1 - m_2)/(1 + m_1 m_2)|$.

nodes.label: Internal division of a line segment
nodes.title: Point dividing segment $AB$ internally in ratio $a:b$ has coordinates $\left(\frac{b x_1 + a x_2}{a+b}, \frac{b y_1 + a y_2}{a+b}\right)$.

nodes.label: Median of a triangle
nodes.title: Segment joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

nodes.label: Centroid of a triangle
nodes.title: Intersection point of the medians, located at the average of vertices' coordinates.

nodes.label: Circumcentre of a triangle
nodes.title: Point of concurrency of perpendicular bisectors of sides, center of circumscribed circle.

nodes.label: Orthocentre of a triangle
nodes.title: Point of concurrency of altitudes (perpendiculars from vertices to opposite sides).

nodes.label: Area of a triangle using coordinate vertices
nodes.title: Area = $1/2 |x_1 y_2 - x_2 y_1|$ when one vertex is at origin, with translation as needed.

nodes.label: Equation of a circle centered at $(h,k)$
nodes.title: Equation $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$ defines circle with center $(h,k)$ and radius $r$.

nodes.label: Equation of a circle in general form
nodes.title: Form $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c=0$, center $(-g,-f)$, radius $\sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$.

nodes.label: Points relative to circle (inside, on, outside)
nodes.title: Determined by comparing distance from center to point against radius.

nodes.label: Equation of tangent to circle at a point
nodes.title: Line perpendicular to radius at point of tangency, slope is negative reciprocal of radius slope.

nodes.label: Equation of tangent lines parallel/perpendicular to a given line
nodes.title: Lines parallel share slope; perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals.

nodes.label: Tangents to circle from an external point
nodes.title: Two tangents possible; their slopes satisfy perpendicular distance equal to radius.

nodes.label: Length of tangent from a point to a circle
nodes.title: Length calculated via Pythagorean theorem using radius and distance from point to center.

nodes.label: Tangents to two circles: external and internal touching
nodes.title: Condition for touching: distance between centers equals sum or difference of radii.

nodes.label: Common chord of two circles
nodes.title: Line given by difference of circle equations passes through intersection points of circles.

nodes.label: Average rate of change
nodes.title: Slope of the secant line between two points on a function over an interval.

nodes.label: Limit of a function
nodes.title: The value that a function approaches as the input approaches a certain point.

nodes.label: Continuity of a function
nodes.title: Function is continuous at $x = a$ if $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)$ and graph is unbroken there.

nodes.label: Derivative from first principles
nodes.title: Limit definition of derivative: $\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$.

nodes.label: Differentiation rules: power rule
nodes.title: Derivative of $x^n$ is $n x^{n-1}$ for real $n$.

nodes.label: Differentiation rules: sum and difference
nodes.title: Derivative of sum/difference is sum/difference of derivatives.

nodes.label: Product rule
nodes.title: Derivative of $uv$ is $u \frac{dv}{dx} + v \frac{du}{dx}$.

nodes.label: Quotient rule
nodes.title: Derivative of $\frac{u}{v}$ is $\frac{v \frac{du}{dx} - u \frac{dv}{dx}}{v^2}$.

nodes.label: Chain rule
nodes.title: Derivative of composite $y=f(g(x))$ is $f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)$.

nodes.label: Second derivatives
nodes.title: The derivative of the first derivative, representing rate of change of slope.

nodes.label: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Basic derivatives: $\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x)=\cos x$, $\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x)= -\sin x$, $\frac{d}{dx}(\tan x)=\sec^2 x$.

nodes.label: Derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Derivatives of arcsin, arccos, arctan functions with standard formulas involving square roots and denominators.

nodes.label: Derivatives of exponential functions
nodes.title: For $y=e^x$, derivative is $e^x$; for $y=a^x$, derivative involves $a^x \ln a$.

nodes.label: Derivatives of logarithmic functions
nodes.title: Derivative of $\ln x$ is $1/x$, and of $\log_a x$ involves natural logs and chain rule.

nodes.label: Trigonometric identities
nodes.title: Basic identities including Pythagorean, reciprocal, quotient identities.

nodes.label: Compound angle formulae
nodes.title: Formulas for $\sin (A \pm B), \cos (A \pm B), \tan (A \pm B)$ expressed via trigonometric functions of angles $A$ and $B$.

nodes.label: Double angle formulae
nodes.title: Formulas for $\sin 2A, \cos 2A, \tan 2A$ derived from compound angle identities.

nodes.label: Sum to product and product to sum formulae
nodes.title: Transformations expressing sums/differences of sines/cosines as products and vice versa.

nodes.label: Inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.title: Functions $\sin^{-1}, \cos^{-1}, \tan^{-1}$ mapping ratios back to angles.

nodes.label: Permutation
nodes.title: Counting arrangements of objects where order matters.

nodes.label: Factorial notation
nodes.title: Notation $n!$ representing product of all positive integers up to $n$.

nodes.label: Combination
nodes.title: Counting selections of objects where order does not matter, given by $C(n,r)$ or $\binom{n}{r}$.

nodes.label: Fundamental principle of counting
nodes.title: If one task can be done in $m$ ways and another in $n$ ways, then both can be done in $m \times n$ ways.

nodes.label: Elementary probability
nodes.title: Calculation of probability as favorable outcomes over total possible outcomes.

nodes.label: Sample space
nodes.title: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.

nodes.label: Mutually exclusive events
nodes.title: Events that cannot occur simultaneously; probability of union is sum of probabilities.

nodes.label: Addition rule for probability
nodes.title: Probability of $A$ or $B$ is $P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$ for overlapping events.

nodes.label: Exhaustive events
nodes.title: A set of events that covers all possible outcomes; sum of probabilities equals 1.

nodes.label: Venn diagrams in probability
nodes.title: Visual representation of events and their intersections and unions.

nodes.label: Independent events
nodes.title: Events where occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other.

nodes.label: Multiplication law for independent events
nodes.title: Probability of both $A$ and $B$ occurring is $P(A) \times P(B)$ if independent.

nodes.label: Conditional probability
nodes.title: Probability of event $A$ occurring given event $B$ has occurred: $P(A|B) = P(A \cap B)/P(B)$.
